scope: V7 literature, novelty, and pinned-V6 audit evidence; targeted rather than exhaustive

methods.bibliography: DOIs and dates were checked against NCBI PubMed/PMC, publisher pages, and Crossref records. Claims were read from primary abstracts or full text.
methods.forward_citations: Targeted forward-citation candidates were discovered with OpenAlex and retained only after the later work was checked against a primary publisher, PubMed, or PMC record.
methods.repository: The clean published repository dist/github-repository was read at commit 9e95c6ce2e21587f9dbe2d18dcb5ab7787b140f6. Critical source blobs were compared with the primary working repository and published HEAD.
methods.limitations: No exhaustive citation-network review and no independent rerun of V6 sweeps was performed. An unlocated precedent is not evidence of absence.

literature_sources.authors: Herbert A. Simon
literature_sources.title: A mechanism for social selection and successful altruism
literature_sources.claim_boundary: Precedence for docility as receptivity to social influence whose gross fitness benefit can carry an altruistic cost under bounded rationality; not a model of V7's separated factual, behavioral, approval, and normative channels.

literature_sources.authors: Alberto Acerbi; Magnus Enquist; Stefano Ghirlanda
literature_sources.title: Cultural evolution and individual development of openness and conservatism
literature_sources.claim_boundary: Direct precedence for cultural transmission modifying the propensity for later social learning and for age-related openness/conservatism; not authority-specific conflict override.

literature_sources.authors: Maxime Derex; Jean-Francois Bonnefon; Robert Boyd; Alex Mesoudi
literature_sources.title: Causal understanding is not necessary for the improvement of culturally evolving technology
literature_sources.verification: Publisher DOI and Crossref; later primary articles explicitly cite it
literature_sources.claim_boundary: Shows improvement in its transmission-chain task without increasing causal understanding; does not show that understanding is never useful.

literature_sources.authors: Ali Seyhun Saral; Paula Ibanez de Aldecoa; Maxime Derex
literature_sources.title: The roles of cultural transmission and causal reasoning in the cultural evolution of technology
literature_sources.claim_boundary: Across two transmission-chain experiments, cultural transmission improved performance without causal structure; causal reasoning accelerated early improvement and its effect diminished later.

literature_sources.authors: David Schultner; Lucas Molleman; Bjorn Lindstrom
literature_sources.title: Feature-based reward learning shapes human social learning strategies
literature_sources.verification: NCBI PMC/PubMed, publisher page, and Crossref
literature_sources.claim_boundary: Six experiments and agent-based simulations support a domain-general reward-learning account of flexible social-learning strategies; it is a mandatory strong comparator, not proof that specialized biases never exist.

literature_sources.authors: Ludovic Maisonneuve; Laurent Lehmann; Charles Mullon
literature_sources.title: The coevolution of learning schedules and teaching enhances cumulative knowledge and drives a teacher-innovator syndrome
literature_sources.venue: Proceedings of the Royal Society B 292(2040):20242470
literature_sources.claim_boundary: Direct theoretical precedence for coevolving lifetime learning schedules, parental teaching, cumulative knowledge, and teacher-innovator versus scrounger specialization.

literature_sources.authors: Alejandro Perez Velilla; Paul E. Smaldino
literature_sources.title: A demographic theory of similarity-biased social learning
literature_sources.claim_boundary: Models costly individual learning, copying, tag informativeness, demographic composition, and frequency-dependent invasion barriers. Age cohort is an explicit application of the tag logic, not a full age-structured life-history model.

literature_sources.authors: Frederick Callaway et al.
literature_sources.title: Rational use of cognitive resources in human planning
literature_sources.claim_boundary: Supports a resource-rational metareasoning comparator for finite planning operations; it is not itself a social-learning or deference model.

literature_sources.authors: Alex Mesoudi; Alex Thornton
literature_sources.title: What is cumulative cultural evolution?
literature_sources.venue: Proceedings of the Royal Society B 285:20180712
literature_sources.claim_boundary: Defines and separates criteria for cumulative cultural evolution; increasing stored statements or confidence alone is insufficient.

literature_sources.authors: Daniel Deffner; Richard McElreath
literature_sources.title: When does selection favor learning from the old? Social learning in age-structured populations
literature_sources.claim_boundary: Direct precedence for age-structured social learning, copy-old/copy-young biases, environmental change, demographic filtering, and adult updating.

literature_sources.authors: T. J. H. Morgan; L. E. Rendell; M. Ehn; W. Hoppitt; K. N. Laland
literature_sources.title: The evolutionary basis of human social learning
literature_sources.venue: Proceedings of the Royal Society B 279(1729):653-662
literature_sources.claim_boundary: Empirical precedence for adaptive integration of social and asocial information as a function of demonstrator number, consensus, confidence, difficulty, costs, and performance.

literature_sources.authors: Luke Rendell et al.
literature_sources.title: Why copy others? Insights from the social learning strategies tournament
literature_sources.verification: Primary article PDF and DOI metadata
literature_sources.claim_boundary: Direct precedent for competing selective social-learning strategies in changing environments and for behavior filtering by demonstrators.

literature_sources.authors: Maxime Derex; Jean-Francois Bonnefon; Robert Boyd; Richard McElreath; Alex Mesoudi
literature_sources.title: Social learning preserves both useful and useless theories by canalizing learners' exploration
literature_sources.venue: Proceedings of the Royal Society B 292(2039):20242499
literature_sources.verification: Royal Society publisher page and Crossref
literature_sources.claim_boundary: Experimentally shows that transmitted theories can canalize exploration and persist whether accurate or misleading; this is ordinary social learning and does not by itself establish authority deference or normative commitment.

literature_sources.authors: Ali Seyhun Saral; Manvir Singh; Antoine Jacquet; Haneul Jang; Maxime Derex
literature_sources.title: Cognitive appeal promotes the persistence of inefficient solutions and hinders cumulative cultural evolution
literature_sources.claim_boundary: A preregistered transmission-chain experiment shows that content appeal can preserve costly ineffective solutions by constraining exploration. It does not require authority, approval, or a bundled useful-plus-useless package.

literature_sources.authors: Talib El Aissati et al.
literature_sources.title: Locals know more than it seems: a new method for revealing collective understanding, tested in three African communities
literature_sources.venue: Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society B 381(1948):20240453
literature_sources.verification: NCBI PubMed and Royal Society DOI
literature_sources.claim_boundary: Across farming communities in Morocco, Mali, and Ghana, group review improved the reliability of final causal answers, indicating distributed causal knowledge and selective deference to better answers.

literature_sources.authors: Elena Miu et al.
literature_sources.title: The refinement paradox and cumulative cultural evolution: Complex products of collective improvement favor conformist outcomes, blind copying, and hyper-credulity
literature_sources.claim_boundary: Tournament precedence for high refinement favoring simple copying and for a possible ecology of hyper-credulity. It directly cites Simon but does not separate factual belief, public behavior, and normative commitment.

literature_sources.authors: David T. Schultner; Bjorn R. Lindstrom; Mina Cikara; David M. Amodio
literature_sources.title: Transmission of social bias through observational learning
literature_sources.claim_boundary: Six experiments support value shaping as a route by which observers acquire another actor's group preferences. This is a strong alternative to authority-specific internalization.

literature_sources.authors: Sophie Sowden et al.
literature_sources.title: Quantifying compliance and acceptance through public and private social conformity
literature_sources.claim_boundary: Within-subject public versus private responding separates public compliance from private acceptance, but the small validation sample does not identify durable normative commitment or dogmatism.

literature_sources.authors: Patricia Kanngiesser et al.
literature_sources.title: Children across societies enforce conventional norms but in culturally variable ways
literature_sources.claim_boundary: Third-party correction of a conventional rule appears across eight societies, with culturally variable form. Rule enforcement is a normative behavior and is not evidence of factual dogmatism.

literature_sources.authors: Andrew Whalen; Thomas L. Griffiths; Daphna Buchsbaum
literature_sources.title: Sensitivity to Shared Information in Social Learning
literature_sources.claim_boundary: A Bayesian model and three experiments show sensitivity to shared private data and sequential testimony; provenance-aware social learning is therefore an established comparator.

literature_sources.authors: Belinda Xie; Brett Hayes
literature_sources.title: Sensitivity to Evidential Dependencies in Judgments Under Uncertainty
literature_sources.claim_boundary: Three experiments found belief updating generally insensitive to dependent versus independent testimony, except among a minority whose prior beliefs valued independence; this qualifies rather than cancels L21.

literature_sources.authors: Uri Hertz; Vaughan Bell; Nichola Raihani
literature_sources.title: Trusting and learning from others: immediate and long-term effects of learning from observation and advice
literature_sources.venue: Proceedings of the Royal Society B 288(1961):20211414
literature_sources.claim_boundary: A preregistered experiment distinguishes advice from observed action and immediate from persistent effects; it is a useful message-format comparator, not evidence for normative authority.

literature_sources.authors: Pearl Han Li
literature_sources.title: Weighing first- and second-hand information: How children and adults evaluate sources of moral and factual knowledge across two cultures
literature_sources.claim_boundary: Moral and factual testimony are evaluated differently across age and culture, supporting separate domain labels while warning that developmental and cultural effects are not uniform.

literature_sources.authors: Pieter van den Berg; TuongVan Vu; Lucas Molleman
literature_sources.title: Unpredictable benefits of social information can lead to the evolution of individual differences in social learning
literature_sources.claim_boundary: Evolutionary-model precedence for flexible developmental programs and individual variation when social-information benefits are unpredictable.

forward_citation_checks.result: Later primary articles cite Derex et al. 2019 and materially extend the copying-versus-reasoning question to manipulated causal structure, theory canalization, and content appeal.
Miu et al. 2024 explicitly cites Simon 1990 in its primary PMC reference list while modeling the refinement ecology of blind copying and hyper-credulity.
The later evolutionary model preserves the broad precedence that developmental social-learning flexibility can itself evolve; it does not make authority-specific conflict override redundant.
